subject: physics
title: The Standard Model: Quarks and Leptons
welcome_lead: Sort matter into six quarks, six leptons and their antiparticles.
meta_desc: A-Level Particle Physics adventure on the Standard Model classification of matter.
final_note: Three generations of quarks and leptons make all known matter.

concepts.def: u, d, c, s, t, b — never seen free.
e, μ, τ and their neutrinos.

walkthroughs.body_html: Up (+2/3) and down (-1/3); charm and strange; top and bottom. Only the 1st generation (u, d) is stable in everyday matter — protons and neutrons.
Electron, muon, tau (charge −1) and their neutrinos (charge 0). Leptons feel weak force; charged ones feel EM. They don't feel the strong force.
Each particle has an antiparticle with opposite charge, baryon number and lepton number, but same mass. Positron is anti-electron; antiproton is uud antiquarks.

Which of the following is a fundamental particle: proton, electron, or neutron?
options: It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.
Only the electron — protons and neutrons are made of quarks.
All three (proton, electron, neutron) are fundamental particles that cannot be broken down.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.

mcqs.q: What did Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment show about the atom?
options: It showed that atoms are solid spheres of positive charge with electrons embedded inside.
Most of the atom is empty space, with a tiny dense positive nucleus.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.
It showed that alpha particles can pass through any material because they are massless.

mcqs.q: When does an electron behave as a wave?
options: In experiments that probe wave properties (e.g. diffraction through a crystal); in particle-like experiments it behaves as a particle.
Electrons are always waves and only look like particles at low energy.
Electrons are sometimes waves and sometimes particles depending on the temperature of the apparatus.
Only the proton is fundamental; electrons and neutrons are composite.
